stories.headline: Thinking Machines releases Inkling, a 975B-parameter open-weights multimodal model under Apache 2.0

key_facts.fact: Inkling is a Mixture-of-Experts transformer with 975B total parameters and 41B active, a 1M-token context window, pretrained on 45 trillion tokens of text, images, audio and video.
key_facts.excerpt: Our model, called Inkling, is a Mixture-of-Experts transformer with 975B total parameters, 41B active. It supports a context window of up to 1M tokens. It was pretrained on 45 trillion tokens of text, images, audio and video.

key_facts.fact: It is the first in-house model from Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab, and unlike flagship models from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google it ships open-weight, released Wednesday July 15, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Thinking Machines Lab, the AI startup founded by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, released its first in-house AI model Wednesday morning, called Inkling. And unlike the flagship models from OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google, it's open-weight, meaning outside developers and companies can download it and modify it directly.

key_facts.fact: Inkling scores 77.6% on SWE-bench Verified, beating US open rival Nvidia Nemotron 3's 71.9%, and 91.4% on VoiceBench versus 94.4% for Gemini 3.1 Pro on high reasoning effort. It is released under an Apache 2.0 license.
key_facts.excerpt: released Inkling, its first major language model under an enterprise-friendly Apache 2.0 open source license, and it boasts high, if sub state-of-the-art, performance for open weights models on third-party benchmarks, specifically software engineering (77.6% on SWE-bench Verified, where it beats fellow U.S. open rival Nvidia Nemotron 3's 71.9%) and voice understanding (91.4% on VoiceBench compared to 94.4% for Gemini 3.1 Pro on high reasoning effort).

key_facts.fact: The MoE design largely follows DeepSeek-V3: each MoE layer contains 256 routed experts and 2 shared experts, with 6 routed experts activated per token, using a sigmoid-based router with auxiliary-loss-free load balancing.
key_facts.excerpt: The MoE design largely follows DeepSeek-V3. Each MoE layer contains 256 routed experts and 2 shared experts, with 6 routed experts ... per token. Inkling uses a sigmoid-based router with an auxiliary-loss-free load-balancing bias.

key_facts.fact: Alongside Inkling the company previewed Inkling-Small, a 276B-parameter MoE model with 12B active parameters that matches or exceeds its larger sibling on many benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: Alongside Inkling we are sharing a preview of Inkling-Small, a 276B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model (12B active, vs. 41B for Inkling) with a different performance/latency trade-off. Inkling-Small matches or exceeds its larger sibling on many benchmarks.

key_facts.fact: Weights are downloadable on Hugging Face; the model is available on Tinker with 64K and 256K context options at a 50% discount for a limited time.
key_facts.excerpt: Inkling is available on Tinker today with context length options of 64K and 256K tokens. We are offering Inkling at a 50% discount for a limited time, with full pricing information available in our documentation.

key_facts.fact: The model card lists a release date of July 15, 2026 and describes a 66-layer decoder-only transformer that is natively multimodal on input, with images encoded via a hierarchical patch encoder and audio via discrete token encoding.
key_facts.excerpt: #### Date of release ... July 15, 2026 ... A 66-layer decoder-only transformer with a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) feed-forward backbone: each token is routed to 6 of 256 experts, plus 2 shared experts active on every token.

stories.headline: OpenAI unveils GPT-Red, a self-play red-teaming model that beat human testers 84% to 13%

key_facts.fact: GPT-Red is an automated red-teaming model trained to find prompt injection vulnerabilities at scale so OpenAI can fix them before wider deployment.
key_facts.excerpt: We trained GPT-Red, an automated red-teaming model that scales our ability to find vulnerabilities so we can fix them before wider deployment.

key_facts.fact: GPT-Red is trained with self-play reinforcement learning: the attacker model and a collection of diverse defender LLMs train simultaneously, with GPT-Red rewarded for eliciting failures and defenders rewarded for resisting.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-Red is trained using self-play reinforcement learning, where the model and a collection of diverse defender LLMs are trained simultaneously on a broad set of red-teaming scenarios. GPT-Red is rewarded for eliciting a valid failure, such as a successful prompt injection, while the defender models are rewarded for resisting the attack and completing their original tasks.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI trained GPT-Red at the compute scale of some of its largest post-training runs, which it calls an unprecedented amount of compute dedicated purely to improving safety.
key_facts.excerpt: We trained GPT-Red at the compute scale of some of our largest post-training runs at OpenAI—an unprecedented amount of compute dedicated purely for improving safety.

key_facts.fact: By the end of training GPT-Red could break nearly all models it was pitted against, including production models up to and including GPT-5.5; its attacks were then used to adversarially train GPT-5.6.
key_facts.excerpt: At the end of its training, GPT-Red is a very strong attacker: it can break nearly all models it is pitted against, both internal and production models up to and including GPT-5.5. After GPT-Red completed training, we used it to generate prompt injections for the training of GPT-5.6, resulting in the model becoming highly resistant to GPT-Red's attacks.

key_facts.fact: On an independent benchmark of scenarios it had not seen in training, GPT-Red found successful attack paths in 84% of cases versus 13% for human security researchers running the same challenge.
key_facts.excerpt: When OpenAI ran GPT-Red against the same scenarios — scenarios the model had not seen during training — it succeeded on 84% of them. The human red-teamers had succeeded on 13%.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says GPT-Red discovered a previously unseen attack type it calls a 'fake chain of thought', inserting a fake entry into another model's reasoning trace to trick it into acting on spoofed information.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI claims that GPT-Red found a type of prompt injection attack that the researchers had not seen before, which they call a fake chain of thought... GPT-Red found a way to insert a fake entry into another model's chain of thought that would trick that model into acting on spoofed information.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI researcher Dylan Hunn said the model systematically varies attacks it discovers: 'Compared to a human red-teamer, the model is very, very good at finding exactly what will work, exactly what's most effective.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Compared to a human red-teamer, the model is very, very good at finding exactly what will work, exactly what's most effective," Hunn said. "It's extremely persistent about drilling down into an attack that it has discovered."

stories.headline: Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs launch AI bioresilience program for pathogen surveillance

key_facts.fact: Google DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs published a joint approach to bioresilience on July 16, 2026, covering prevention, detection and response to biological threats.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, Google DeepMind and [Isomorphic Labs](https://www.isomorphiclabs.com/) are sharing our [joint approach to bioresilience]

key_facts.fact: DeepMind's AlphaEvolve agent can optimize the algorithms used to produce and analyze metagenomic sequencing data, making DNA analysis quicker and cheaper so outbreaks can be detected faster at large scale.
key_facts.excerpt: We are helping make pathogen surveillance more cost-effective. For example, our agent AlphaEvolve can optimize algorithms used for producing and analyzing metagenomic sequencing data, helping detect new outbreaks faster. This optimization allows for quicker and more accurate DNA analysis, making it cheaper to track diseases worldwide on a large scale.

key_facts.fact: Isomorphic Labs has established a focused unit to rapidly deploy its drug design engine to design medical countermeasures for both naturally occurring pandemics and risks arising from misuse of advanced AI.
key_facts.excerpt: To support government bodies and non-profit organizations during novel outbreaks, Isomorphic Labs has established a focused unit to rapidly deploy its drug design engine to design medical countermeasures that could address both naturally occurring pandemics and potential risks arising from the misuse of advanced AI.

key_facts.fact: The companies are exploring how AlphaGenome and protein function annotation could detect and characterize pathogens from sequence data, identifying emerging threats faster than traditional methods.
key_facts.excerpt: We are also exploring how technologies like AlphaGenome and Protein Function annotation could be used to help detect and characterize pathogens from sequence data, identifying novel patterns and emerging threats faster than traditional methods.

key_facts.fact: The companies frame AI as both a source of biosecurity risk and a critical tool for response, citing shifting ecosystems, global travel and the potential misuse of AI.
key_facts.excerpt: The global biosecurity landscape is rapidly evolving. Shifting natural ecosystems, global travel and the potential misuse of AI require greater vigilance — yet AI is also a critical tool for our response.

key_facts.fact: Over the past year the partnership has engaged more than 15 government agencies, biosecurity organizations and research groups, and grants trusted researchers access to its latest AI systems.
key_facts.excerpt: Over the past year, the partnership has engaged with more than 15 government agencies, biosecurity organizations, and research groups to implement these solutions... DeepMind and Isomorphic Labs are granting trusted researchers access to their latest AI systems.

key_facts.excerpt: The lawsuit, filed in the US District Court for the Northern District of Texas, alleges that South Carolina's Terry Wayne Harwood violated xAI's Terms of Service and Acceptable Use Policy by exploiting Grok's image-generation capabilities to transform non-sexual photographs into sexually explicit images without the knowledge or consent of those depicted.

key_facts.fact: It marks one of the first known legal actions by an AI company against one of its own users over the alleged creation of illegal AI-generated sexual content.
key_facts.excerpt: marking one of the first known legal actions by an AI company against a user over the alleged creation of illegal AI-generated sexual content.

key_facts.fact: The complaint alleges Harwood created multiple xAI accounts and used 'misleading prompts' to bypass Grok's built-in safety mechanisms designed to prevent generation of explicit material involving minors.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the lawsuit, Harwood created multiple xAI accounts and used what the company described as "misleading prompts" to bypass Grok's built-in safety mechanisms designed to prevent the generation of explicit material involving minors.

key_facts.fact: xAI alleges Harwood uploaded non-sexual images of both adults and minors and attempted to use Grok to generate sexually explicit deepfakes, including child sexual abuse material.
key_facts.excerpt: The complaint alleges that Harwood uploaded non-sexual images of both adults and minors and attempted to use the AI system to generate sexually explicit deepfakes, including child sexual abuse material.

key_facts.fact: Harwood was arrested earlier this year on charges related to the material; the suit was filed on July 15, 2026.

stories.headline: Meta will alert parents when teens discuss suicide or self-harm with its AI chatbot

key_facts.fact: Meta announced on Thursday July 16 that it will notify parents if their teen discusses suicide or self-harm with the Meta AI chatbot, and is working on the ability to contact emergency services when conversations suggest risk of self-harm.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta announced on Thursday that it will now notify parents if their teen discusses suicide or self-harm with the company's Meta AI chatbot. Meta says it's also working on the ability to contact emergency services if someone's conversations suggest they may be at risk of self-harm.

key_facts.fact: Meta says it built a dedicated AI system to identify conversations where a teen makes a clear reference to hurting themselves, and every chat flagged by that AI is manually reviewed before an alert is sent.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta says it has built a dedicated AI system to identify conversations where a teen makes a clear reference to hurting themselves... "That's why, as we continue to improve our detection, all chats flagged by our AI will be manually reviewed before an alert is sent."

key_facts.fact: Meta says it will err on the side of caution when a teen's intent is ambiguous: 'While that means we may sometimes notify parents when there may not be real cause for concern, we feel this is the right starting point.'
key_facts.excerpt: "If a teen's intent is ambiguous, we'll err on the side of caution and alert the parent. While that means we may sometimes notify parents when there may not be real cause for concern, we feel this is the right starting point, and we'll continue to monitor to help make sure we're in the right place."

key_facts.fact: The alerts are live now for parents using Instagram Parental Supervision in the US, UK, Australia and Canada, and will roll out globally by the end of the year.
key_facts.excerpt: These alerts are now live for parents using Instagram Parental Supervision in the U.S., U.K., Australia, and Canada, and will roll out globally by the end of the year, Meta says.

key_facts.fact: Meta's 'Limited Content' setting, which places teens in a more restrictive Instagram experience, now applies to Meta AI as well, making the chatbot decline a broader range of prompts.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta also announced that its "Limited Content" setting—which lets parents place their teens in a more restrictive experience on Instagram—now applies to Meta AI as well... the Limited Content setting expands those safeguards by making the chatbot decline a broader range of prompts.

key_facts.fact: The changes arrive as Meta and other tech companies face scrutiny from regulators and parents over how AI chatbots respond to users in crisis, a liability question shaping how AI companies design and market products.
key_facts.excerpt: These changes arrive as Meta and other tech companies face scrutiny from regulators and parents over how AI chatbots respond to users in crisis, particularly teenagers —a liability question that's increasingly shaping how AI companies design and market their products.

stories.headline: TSMC posts record Q2 profit up 77%, raises 2026 growth outlook above 40% and capex to $64B

key_facts.fact: TSMC's Q2 net income hit a record NT$706.56 billion (~$21.98 billion), up 77.4% year over year and far above Bloomberg estimates of NT$623.73 billion — a fifth straight quarter of record profit.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC's net income for the three months to June 30 hit a record high of T$706.56 billion ($21.98 billion), much higher than Bloomberg estimates of T$623.73 billion. The figure was a 77.4% jump from the same period a year ago, and marked a fifth straight quarter of record-high profits for the chipmaker.

key_facts.fact: Quarterly revenue was a record NT$1.27 trillion (~$39-40.2 billion), up 36% year over year and at the high end of guidance, with gross margin of 67.7% beating the company's own forecast.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC said second-quarter revenue rose to $40.2 billion, topping the company's guidance range and coming in slightly above the $39.94 billion analyst forecast, while gross margin reached 67.7%, above expectations.

key_facts.fact: TSMC raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook to slightly above 40% in US dollar terms, up from a prior forecast of over 30%.
key_facts.excerpt: Wei said TSMC's 2026 revenue is now expected to increase by more than 40% in U.S. dollar terms, higher than prior forecasts for growth of over 30%.

key_facts.fact: The company lifted 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $60-$64 billion from $52-$56 billion, a record high and roughly a 14% increase.
key_facts.excerpt: Meanwhile, the company also significantly raised its full-year capital expenditure budget from the previous $52 billion to $56 billion to $60 billion to $64 billion, representing an increase of approximately 14% and hitting a record high.

key_facts.fact: About 70-80% of the 2026 capital budget goes to advanced process technologies, 10% to specialty nodes and 10-20% to advanced packaging, testing and mask making.
key_facts.excerpt: About 70–80% of that will go to advanced process technologies, with 10% for specialty nodes and 10–20% for advanced packaging, testing, and mask making.

key_facts.fact: CEO C.C. Wei said 'The AI megatrend is stronger and stronger,' citing a 'very big' gap between customer demand and supply, and said agentic AI is reviving CPU demand.
key_facts.excerpt: Chairman and CEO C.C. Wei cited surging AI demand, including the rise of agentic AI that is reviving CPU demand, as the overwhelming driver. "The AI megatrend is stronger and stronger," Wei said, adding that the company's multi-year conviction is "very high." ... The aggressive spending commitments reflect what Wei called a "very big" gap between customer demand and supply.

key_facts.fact: TSMC shares closed at $419.48 but fell 1.55% in after-hours trading to $412.99 as investors weighed heavier spending and a forecast for lower margins in the current quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares were little changed during the regular session, closing at $419.48, but fell 1.55% in after-hours trading to $412.99 as investors weighed the company's heavier spending plans and a forecast for lower margins in the current quarter.

stories.headline: Hyundai takes 100% of Boston Dynamics as SoftBank exercises put option on its 9.65% stake

key_facts.fact: Hyundai Motor Group disclosed on July 16 that it will make Boston Dynamics a wholly owned subsidiary by acquiring SoftBank Group's stake of around 10%, a move it says will help deploy advanced robotics across its operations.
key_facts.excerpt: SEOUL, July 16 : Hyundai Motor Group on Thursday disclosed that it would make U.S. robotics company Boston Dynamics a wholly owned subsidiary by acquiring SoftBank Group's stake of around 10 per cent, a move it said would help it deploy advanced robotics across its operations.

key_facts.fact: SoftBank exercised a put option on its 9.65% stake under a 2020 contract; terms were not disclosed, but local media reported the transaction would likely be worth about 500 billion won ($335 million).
key_facts.excerpt: Hyundai Motor Group announced on July 16 that Japan's SoftBank exercised its put option (right to sell common shares) for its 9.65% stake in Boston Dynamics, in accordance with a contract signed in 2020.

key_facts.fact: Terms were not disclosed; local media reported the deal would likely be worth about 500 billion won ($335 million), and Kiwoom Securities analyst Shin Yoonchul said the price implied a valuation of about 5 trillion won for Boston Dynamics.
key_facts.excerpt: Terms of the deal were not disclosed. Local media reported last month that the transaction would likely be worth about 500 billion won ($335 million). ... Shin Yoonchul, an analyst at Kiwoom Securities, said the transaction price implied a valuation of about 5 trillion won for Boston Dynamics.

key_facts.fact: Hyundai acquired an 80% controlling stake in Boston Dynamics from SoftBank in 2021 for about 1 trillion won ($671 million); the current structure is Hyundai Motor 28%, Chairman Euisun Chung 22.6%, Kia 17.2%, Hyundai Mobis 11.3%, Hyundai Glovis 11.25%.
key_facts.excerpt: The current ownership structure is Hyundai Motor with 28%, Kia with 17.2%, Hyundai Mobis with 11.3%, Hyundai Glovis with 11.25%, Hyundai Motor Group Chairman Euisun Chung with 22.6%, and SoftBank with 9.65%. ... Hyundai Motor Group has come to hold a 100% stake about five years after completing the acquisition of a controlling stake (80%) in Boston Dynamics from Japan's SoftBank for 1 trillion won (about $671 million) in 2021.

key_facts.fact: Boston Dynamics is pushing commercialization of the Atlas humanoid with a mass-production goal of 2028, and Hyundai is reviewing an IPO including a US Nasdaq listing.
key_facts.excerpt: Boston Dynamics is pushing for the commercialization of the humanoid robot Atlas and is expanding related businesses with the goal of mass production in 2028. ... Hyundai Motor Group is also reported to be reviewing an Initial Public Offering (IPO), including a listing of Boston Dynamics on the US Nasdaq market, from various angles.

key_facts.fact: Hyundai Motor shares have fallen more than 30% since local media first reported the plan last month; the stock closed down 2.1% on Thursday against a 6.4% decline for the KOSPI benchmark.
key_facts.excerpt: Hyundai Motor shares have fallen more than 30 per cent since local media first reported last month that the automaker planned to buy SoftBank's remaining stake in Boston Dynamics. On Thursday, Hyundai Motor shares closed down 2.1 per cent, compared with a 6.4 per cent decline for the benchmark KOSPI.

key_facts.fact: The put option was tied to a condition that SoftBank could sell its remaining stake if a US IPO did not take place by June 2026.

key_facts.fact: Fed Governor Lisa Cook said on July 15 that risks 'continue to be strongly weighted toward higher inflation,' that she voted to keep rates steady last month because tariffs and the Middle East conflict should produce only short-lived inflation increases, and that the 'data center buildout has added some heat to the economy.'
key_facts.excerpt: I voted with the rest of the FOMC last month to keep rates steady. I supported this stance, because the two main factors that have pushed up inflation over the past year—tariffs and the conflict in the Middle East—should, in theory, result in only short-lived increases in inflation... Going forward, though, I believe the risks continue to be strongly weighted toward higher inflation... data center buildout has added some heat to the economy.

key_facts.fact: Cook noted GDP growth in 2025 came in at 2.0 percent and FOMC participants now forecast 2.2 percent for 2026 — both about half a percentage point above last year's forecasts — with labor productivity growing about 2-1/2 percent per year over the past two years. The FOMC next meets in two weeks.
key_facts.excerpt: GDP growth in 2025 came in at 2.0 percent, and FOMC participants now forecast that 2026 will come in at 2.2 percent. Both readings exceed last year's forecasts by about 1/2 percentage point. Labor productivity is booming, having grown about 2-1/2 percent per year over the past two years... I look forward to engaging with my fellow Committee members at our next meeting in two weeks.

key_facts.fact: At its June 17 meeting the FOMC maintained the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent.

stories.headline: Brokerage infrastructure firm Alpaca raises $435M led by Peak XV to push into prime brokerage

key_facts.fact: Alpaca announced on July 16 a $135 million equity raise led by Peak XV with major participation from Elefund; total new financing reaches $435 million including debt financing primarily from Payward (Kraken's parent) and BMO.
key_facts.excerpt: Alpaca, a global leader in agent-first brokerage infrastructure, today announced a $135 million raise led by Peak XV, with major participation from Elefund... The new financing totals $435 million, inclusive of debt financing primarily from Payward, the parent company of global digital asset platform Kraken, and BMO.

key_facts.fact: The round follows Alpaca's $150 million Series D announced in January 2026, which valued the company at $1.15 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The financing builds on significant business growth as tokenization and AI reshape the industry, following Alpaca's $150 million Series D announced in January 2026, which valued the company at $1.15 billion

key_facts.fact: Alpaca said it has doubled revenue year over year for three consecutive years, surpassed $1.5 billion in assets under custody backing tokenized equities, and saw monthly active API users grow nearly 4x in the last six months.
key_facts.excerpt: Doubled revenue year over year for three consecutive years. Surpassed $1.5 billion in AUC for the underlying stocks backing tokenized equities. Monthly active API users grew nearly 4x during the last six months as Alpaca expanded agentic AI capabilities.

key_facts.fact: Alpaca will use the financing to accelerate its agent-first brokerage and API-first prime brokerage infrastructure; CEO Yoshi Yokokawa said Alpaca is 'uniquely positioned to become the default infrastructure layer for tokenized global capital markets and AI-native financial services.'
key_facts.excerpt: Alpaca will use the new financing to accelerate its agent-first brokerage and API-first prime brokerage infrastructure, enabling financial companies and institutional clients to build and scale investing products across traditional and onchain markets... 'Alpaca is uniquely positioned to become the default infrastructure layer for tokenized global capital markets and AI-native financial services,' said Yoshi Yokokawa, Co-Founder and CEO of Alpaca.

key_facts.fact: The company acquired an IFSCA-regulated broker-dealer in GIFT City India and UK/European regulated entities, completing passporting in all 30 EEA countries; it now supports over 10 million brokerage accounts across hundreds of fintechs and institutions in more than 40 countries.
key_facts.excerpt: Acquired an IFSCA-regulated broker-dealer and payment service provider in GIFT City, establishing Alpaca's regulated presence in India. Acquired UK and European regulated entities and completed passporting in all 30 EEA countries... Today, Alpaca supports over 10 million brokerage accounts across hundreds of fintechs and institutions in more than 40 countries, backed by $400 million in funding.

key_facts.fact: Alpaca is exploring entry into prime broking with the $435 million raise.
